qc.label_under_test: A space-initial byte-fallback token: a space followed by a non-ASCII character such as '÷', a CJK character or an accented capital ('Ú'); quiet when the same content is written in ASCII.

neighbours.label: A space-led split-byte token: a space merged with the lead byte of a character the tokenizer breaks into bytes. Fires for Latin-1 symbols and letters after a space (÷ × ß ø Þ ð ú Ú) and for CJK characters in the U+6000-6FFF block (源 慈 欧 洗); quiet for emoji, Cyrillic, Greek, Korean, other CJK blocks (e.g. 鬱 蠡), accented letters inside words, and ASCII twins.
fire: Compute 12 ÷ 4 on the board before the bell rings.
In German, the letter ß is called Eszett.
The Danish letter ø appears in many place names.
Old English scribes used the letter Þ for the th sound.
Icelandic still writes ð in many everyday words.
The sign by the harbor read Úlfur Hall.
In Spanish, the word tú carries an accent, and teachers say ú marks the stress.
quiet: Compute 12 / 4 on the board before the bell rings.
The storage room measures 3 x 5 meters.
In German, the letters ss are called a double s.
The Greek letter λ appears in many formulas.
Old English scribes used the letters th for that sound.
Russian still writes ж in many everyday words.
The sign by the harbor read Ulfur Hall.
In French, the word café carries an accent that marks the stress.

predictions: Expect 6-8 of 8 fire sentences above 0.2 (Latin-1 symbols were 0.5-0.9 in my exploration); risk is the ASCII twins: '12 / 4' and '3 x 5' may reach ~0.25 on a lone space token, and ú/Ú/ø may be whole tokens in some frames.
